decisive_items: a 2-cm sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm
diffuse homogeneous enhancement after contrast administration
The lesion was predominantly isointense to gray matter on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on T2-weighted images
response.rationale: Pituitary adenoma is the most common sellar/suprasellar mass with homogeneous enhancement and typical clinical presentation (bitemporal hemianopsia, mild hyperprolactinemia). Lymphocytic hypophysitis can mimic but is less likely given subacute onset and no pituitary stalk thickening or inflammatory context.

rejected.why: Craniopharyngioma often has calcifications and cystic components; imaging shows homogeneous enhancement, less typical.
Meningioma usually arises from dura and may show dural tail; less likely in sellar location without dural attachment.
Lymphocytic hypophysitis can present similarly but is more common in peripartum women and often shows stalk thickening; less likely here.
